name: setup_status
description: Checklist of what is configured, missing or degraded. Call at the start of every run.

name: record_setup_decision
description: Record the user decision for an amber setup item (e.g. "no browser, accepted"), so setup can complete.

decision.description: The user's decision, in their words

name: start_run
description: Start a run and record detected capabilities (connectors, browser, local folder). Returns run_id.

capabilities.description: {connectors: {gmail, calendar, linkedin}, browser: "claude-in-chrome" | "built-in" | null, local_folder: bool}

name: finish_run
description: Close a run with a one-paragraph summary.

name: get_profile
description: All config sections: filters, prefs, writing, accounts, autonomy, schedule, sources, capabilities.

name: save_config
description: Validate and save one config section. Unknown fields are rejected. Field names and types are in templates/settings.example.yaml; an invalid call returns the section's expected fields.

section.description: filters | prefs | writing | accounts | autonomy | schedule | sources | capabilities

name: get_document
description: Read a user document: profile (CV distilled), stories, reusable-answers, voice.

name: save_document
description: Save a user document (markdown).

name: find_company
description: Dedupe check. Pass url when you have one: an exact URL or ATS posting, under any company and any recorded alias, is checked first and listed in exact_role_ids. Then fuzzy match on name, aliases, domain and ATS slug. verdict: new | seen | skip (live application, same posting, or no_cold_apply). seen is a known company with nothing blocking: a different requisition there is a lead, even after a rejection. skip for a tracked posting is for discovery; to apply to a known queued role, pass its id to gate_check.

name: set_no_cold_apply
description: Mark a company as no_cold_apply (an intro or recruiter process is open), or clear it.

on.description: true to set, false to clear

name: add_alias
description: Add an alias to a company (brand, former name, parent) so dedupe catches it.

name: upsert_role
description: Create or update a role (creates the company if needed). Pass id to update a known role. Otherwise a role is matched on its exact URL or ATS posting, never on title: with no match a new role starts as found, and possible_role_ids lists same-title roles at the company to rule out before scoring. A URL matching several roles, or a second posting ID from the same employer board, returns an error and writes nothing. Returns the find_company dedupe result unless id is given.

company.description: Company name as the employer writes it

company_aliases.description: Other names, e.g. a brand vs the legal entity

url_aliases.description: Other URLs for this same posting, e.g. the LinkedIn card of an Ashby job. Needs identity_evidence

identity_evidence.description: How you confirmed the listings are one posting. Required with url_aliases, and to add an ATS posting from another ATS or employer board to a known role

ats.description: ashby | greenhouse | lever | workable | teamtailor | personio | join | workday | other

location_line.description: Verbatim location line from the employer ATS

industry.description: Industry of the business line the role sits in

name: get_role
description: Role with its company, full event history, artifacts, interviews, and the urls and ATS postings it is known by. A linked duplicate's id returns its canonical role; history, artifacts, interviews and URLs then cover the whole group under their original ids, with requested_role_id, linked_role_ids and links.

name: link_duplicate_role
description: Link a historical duplicate row to the canonical role for the same posting. Nothing is deleted: the duplicate's events, artifacts and interviews show under the canonical role, and its id resolves to that role in every tool. Same company only. Refuses two posting IDs from one employer board, and histories that disagree. A duplicate with only preparatory states links under a role with an application history, or under a preparatory role that moved last. A duplicate with an application history needs the same latest status and outcome on the canonical role, no older (fix it with transition or record first). A duplicate already linked to another role is refused. A canonical role's own duplicates move along when it is linked. Linking the same pair again returns the group.

canonical_role_id.description: The role to keep as the card. A linked duplicate's id stands for its canonical role

duplicate_role_id.description: The other row for the same posting. Its history, artifacts and interviews stay and show under the canonical role

reason.description: Why the two rows are one role

evidence.description: How you confirmed they are the same posting, e.g. both link to the same ATS URL

name: transition
description: Move a role through found → verified → scored → queued → applied → interviewing → offer (dropped from found/verified/scored/queued; closed from queued/applied/interviewing/offer). Rejects illegal moves. verified needs evidence (URL + verbatim location line), location_line and location_type. dropped needs evidence (quote or rule:<id>). applied needs the confirmation text. closed needs outcome.

to.description: found | verified | scored | queued | applied | interviewing | offer | dropped | closed

evidence.description: Verbatim quote with URL, rule:<id>, or confirmation text

category.description: For drops: location | pay | industry | role_shape | stack | culture | duplicate | gated | other

question.description: For queued: the single blocking question for the user

blocked_by.description: For queued: browser | user | login | captcha | other

location_line.description: verified only: verbatim from the ATS

location_type.description: verified only: remote | hybrid | onsite | unknown

score_notes.description: scored only: short notes, including gaps kept internal

name: record
description: Append a validated event without the state-machine check: outcomes from outside (rejection, invite, user decision) or a note (omit status). For a message or board record pass source, source_account, source_id and occurred_at: replaying the same occurrence returns the original event_id (duplicate: true), a changed payload under one id is an error, and the status moves only if it is newer than the role's latest status event and the status machine allows it (status_applied; conflict says why not).

status.description: found | verified | scored | queued | applied | interviewing | offer | dropped | closed (omit for a note)

question.description: Blocking question for the user (shown under Needs you until a later event)

source.description: Events from outside only: where it came from, e.g. gmail, linkedin, board (case-insensitive). Pass with source_account, source_id and occurred_at, or none of them

source_account.description: The mailbox or account, e.g. jobs@example.test. The same source_id in two accounts is two events

source_id.description: The source's own id for this one occurrence (message id; board application id plus its original date), not a thread or a mutable card

occurred_at.description: When it happened, ISO 8601 with an explicit offset (the message date), not when you read it, and not in the future

name: check_pay
description: Deterministic pay-floor check. Drops only if the band maximum is below the floor; straddling bands are kept and flagged. Pass fx_rate when the currency differs from the floor (look it up, never guess).

fx_rate.description: Floor-currency units per 1 unit of currency

name: gate_check
description: Pre-submit check: role verified, not no_cold_apply, no live application at the company, and this posting never applied to before. Any applied, interviewing, offer, rejected or withdrawn event on a row for the posting blocks it, even back in the queue (previous_application, matched_role_id). A posting held by several unlinked roles is blocked until resolved. Call before preparing an application; hooks check again at submit.

name: add_artifact
description: Save a cover note, PDF, Gmail draft id, form answers, confirmation or note. Prose is linted. gmail_draft stays unverified until verify_artifact.

role_id.description: Role id (omit for drafts not tied to a role)

kind.description: cover_note | cover_letter_pdf | gmail_draft | form_answers | confirmation | note

ref.description: Path, URL or Gmail draft id

name: list_artifacts
description: Artifacts for a run, a local day or a role, with lint results and read-back state. The auditor uses this.

date.description: YYYY-MM-DD, a day in filters.timezone (ignored when run_id is given)

name: verify_artifact
description: Mark an artifact verified after reading it back. For gmail_draft, readback must be the get_draft/list_drafts output containing the draft id.

name: lint_prose
description: Lint outbound prose: em/en dashes, "not X but Y", fake-candid openers, volunteered gaps, length.

name: open_items
description: Queue (fresh and stale), unverified drafts, interviews to book, upcoming interviews.

stale_after_days.description: Queue items untouched this long are listed as stale (default 14)

name: pipeline_summary
description: Counts by status, live processes, rejections, queue (fresh and stale).

name: open_board
description: Start the local kanban board (or reuse the running one). With open: true it opens in the user's browser and the link is not returned; otherwise the link is returned. The user drags cards to move roles; moves follow transition's rules and are recorded as the user's. The board stops after 30 idle minutes.

open.description: true also opens it in the default browser. Only when the user asked to see the board now; never in a scheduled run.

name: add_rule
description: Add a user preference or correction as a rule, with reason and example. types says which consumers read it; omit it for global.

reason.description: Why (the incident or the user words)

types.description: Which consumers read it: global | sourcing | scoring | forms | writing | inbox | reporting. Omit for global

name: list_rules
description: Rules with provenance and types, one page at a time: at most 10 by default, limit up to 50. Follow next_cursor until it is null; never act on a partial set. types filters to those consumers plus global rules, which are always included. If rules changed mid-listing, the cursor is refused: restart without it. An entry with requires_detail is too large to list: read it with get_rule. Results stay under 24 KiB, so a page can hold fewer rules than limit; next_cursor says whether more remain.

types.description: Only rules for these consumers (and global ones): global | sourcing | scoring | forms | writing | inbox | reporting. Omit for all

cursor.description: next_cursor from the previous page. Omit types and include_inactive to keep the cursor's

name: get_rule
description: Read one whole rule in chunks. Only for a list_rules entry marked requires_detail. Call until next_cursor is null, join every chunk in order, then JSON.parse the result. Never act on a partial chunk. If rules changed meanwhile, the cursor is refused: restart without it.

id.description: Rule id, from a list_rules entry with requires_detail

cursor.description: next_cursor from the previous chunk. Omit for the first chunk

name: set_rule_types
description: Change which consumers a rule applies to. Edits the classification only: text, reason and who added it stay. Returns the types and rules_revision.

types.description: One or more of: global | sourcing | scoring | forms | writing | inbox | reporting

name: deactivate_rule
description: Deactivate a rule. Repeating it on an inactive rule is a no-op.

name: source_health
description: Per-source status, consecutive failures, yield, and checkpoints: per source account, checked_through (end of the last complete scan; null if none yet), last_coverage and last_attempt_at.

name: set_source_status
description: Record a source result for this run. Three consecutive failures mark it degraded. To also record what a mailbox, calendar or board account scan covered, pass source_account and coverage. complete (needs status ok and checked_through, the actual end of what was read) moves that account's checkpoint forward; partial and unavailable never do. checked_through is the real endpoint: the reader adds its own overlap when it picks the next search window.

source_account.description: Account the scan covered (a mailbox, a board login). Needed with coverage

checked_through.description: How far the scan reached, ISO 8601 with an explicit offset. Needed with complete

coverage.description: complete | partial | unavailable: how much of source_account this run checked

name: add_interview
description: Record an interview, or update one. Omit starts_at for a booking link still to book; the same stage and link again, or interview_id, or the calendar event (source, source_account, source_id and occurred_at together) updates that interview instead of adding one. state: pending | scheduled | cancelled. An applied role moves to interviewing. Returns {interview_id, created, updated, stale, state}; stale means an older update was ignored.

starts_at.description: ISO datetime, omit if not booked yet

interview_id.description: Update this interview (from an earlier call or get_role) instead of adding one. It must belong to role_id

state.description: pending | scheduled | cancelled. Default: scheduled with starts_at, else pending. scheduled needs a time; cancelled records a called-off interview and needs an explicit newer update

source.description: Where the booking came from, e.g. google_calendar. With source_account, source_id and occurred_at

source_id.description: The calendar event or message id; for a recurring event, the occurrence id. A repeat updates the same interview

occurred_at.description: When the event or message happened, ISO 8601 with an explicit offset. An older update than the one applied is ignored

run_id.description: Run id, to attribute the change

name: render_report
description: Markdown daily report. With run_id it covers that run; otherwise the local day. Lead with the outcome via headline. Only read-back drafts and confirmed submissions are claimed.

date.description: YYYY-MM-DD, a day in filters.timezone (report title; ignored for scope when run_id is given)

headline.description: One or two sentences: the outcome

name: audit
description: Post-run rule check for a run (preferred) or a local day: excluded industries, drops without evidence, applied without confirmation, prose lint, drafts not read back, no_cold_apply. Pass run_id or date.

date.description: YYYY-MM-DD, a day in filters.timezone (ignored when run_id is given)

name: import_legacy
description: One-off import of the manual pipeline: applied-log.md, outreach-preferences.md, queue/*.md, and user documents. Pass the contents, or path to a local pipeline/ folder.

path.description: Local path to the pipeline/ folder
